title: What shape has equal opposite sides, and how can we be sure?
description: A four-sided shape has equal opposite sides. A diagonal cuts it into two congruent triangles, and the equal angles that follow are alternate angles. Parallel opposite sides then name the shape.
teaching_notes: One idea: equal opposite sides give congruent triangles by the side side side rule, and the equal angles give parallel sides. Watch for students who name the shape from its look and give no reason.

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 9)
video_script.why: The child knows equal opposite sides from a picture but needs a reason to name the shape.
video_script.substitution: the book's question with opposite sides equal and the hint of a diagonal
video_script.anchor: a four-sided shape ABCD with AB = CD and AD = CB
never_show: right angle marks on the shape
maths_rules: ABCD has AB = CD and AD = CB, and the diagonal BD is drawn
triangle ABD and triangle CDB: AB = CD, AD = CB, BD common, so they are congruent by SSS
angle ABD = angle CDB, alternate angles for AB and DC with transversal BD, so AB || DC
angle ADB = angle CBD, alternate angles for AD and BC with transversal BD, so AD || BC
both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so ABCD is a parallelogram
video_script.design: One idea: congruent triangles give alternate angles, so opposite sides are parallel. One shape and its diagonal stay on the board.

<bookmark mark='cong'/>Two triangles that match exactly are called congruent.

beats.on_screen: Given: ABCD with AB = CD and AD = CB
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eigh B equals C D, and eigh D equals C B.

beats.on_screen: To find: the type of shape ABCD
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find what kind of shape eigh B C D is.

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step one, draw the diagonal B D, which splits the shape into two triangles.

beats.on_screen: AB = CD, AD = CB, BD common: ∆ABD ≅ ∆CDB (three sides)

marks.sides: the three pairs of sides light up

narration: <bookmark mark='sides'/>Step two, eigh B equals C D, eigh D equals C B, and B D is common.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>By the side side side rule, triangle eigh B D is congruent to triangle C D B.

beats.on_screen: ∠ABD = ∠CDB, alternate angles for AB and DC with transversal BD, so AB || DC

marks.match: angle A B D and angle C D B light up
marks.par: A B and D C are marked parallel

narration: <bookmark mark='match'/>Step three, matching angles are equal, so angle eigh B D equals angle C D B.
<bookmark mark='par'/>They are alternate angles for eigh B and D C, with B D as the transversal.
Equal alternate angles mean eigh B is parallel to D C.

marks.match: angle A D B and angle C B D light up
marks.par: A D and B C are marked parallel

narration: <bookmark mark='match'/>Step four, angle eigh D B equals angle C B D in the same way.
<bookmark mark='par'/>They are alternate angles for eigh D and B C, so these two sides are parallel.

beats.on_screen: Check: equal opposite sides, and parallel opposite sides, agree

marks.chk: the given and the result are shown side by side
marks.back: the two statements are linked by an arrow

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step five, check the result against the question.
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, and we also began with both pairs equal.
<bookmark mark='back'/>A shape with both pairs of opposite sides parallel always has equal opposite sides, so the two agree.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>It is a parallelogram.
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
